thread.title: Chinese Internet Weekly: JD.Com In The Spotlight - KraneShares CSI China Internet ETF (NYSEARCA:KWEB)

author: ALT Perspective
title: Chinese Internet Weekly: JD.Com In The Spotlight - KraneShares CSI China Internet ETF (NYSEARCA:KWEB)
text:
Introduction To Chinese Internet Weekly This report aims to discuss the pertinent topics happening in the internet space with a focus on Chinese stocks, starting with the initiation article two weeks ago. Relevant ETFs include the KraneShares CSI China Internet ETF ( KWEB ) and its leveraged version, the Direxion Daily CSI China Internet Index Bull 2x Shares ETF ( CWEB ), as well as the Invesco China Technology ETF ( CQQQ ) and the Global X China Technology ETF ( QQQC ).
Based on the constituents of the top holdings, my preference is towards KWEB. Hence, the companies discussed would tilt towards the top ten holdings of KWEB. Both CQQQ and QQQC named Lenovo Group ( OTCPK:LNVGY , OTCPK:LNVGF ) as one of its top ten holdings. Lenovo is more of a high-tech manufacturer rather than an internet company, the focus of this newsletter. CQQQ also has Sunny Optical ( OTCPK:SNPTF , OTCPK:SOTGY ) within its top ten holdings. Similar to Lenovo, Sunny Optical has a primary listing in Hong Kong. It engages in the design, manufacture, and sale of optical and optical devices products. Sunny Optical is a key supplier to major Chinese smartphone brands Huawei Technologies, Oppo and Vivo. It is also a supplier for Apple's ( AAPL ) iPhones. Again, it hardly qualifies as an internet company.
KWEB Dragged Down By JD.com and Its Second-Tier Holdings In the week ending November 23, 2018, the share price of KWEB fell by 5.3 percent (due to the Thanksgiving break, trading data for November 16 was included to generate the 5-day chart). Of its top five holdings, only JD.com ( JD ) performed worse than KWEB, and it did so by a wide margin. Despite already gaining the most among the top holdings last week, Tencent ( OTCPK:TCEHY , OTCPK:TCTZF ) managed to outperform the rest for the second consecutive week.
KWEB Price data by YCharts
JD.com only represented 5 percent of KWEB by weight as of September 30, 2018. Given that the share price of JD.com has been on the decline continually thereafter, the current weight should be even smaller. Thus, it would be considered unjustified for KWEB to be down 5.3 percent if it was only due to the drag by JD.com, albeit a heavy one.
Looking at the share price movements of the top sixth to tenth stocks by weight, the so-called second-tiered holdings of KWEB, it is easy to see that is indeed not the case. Apart from Ctrip.com ( CTRP ), which experienced its own plunge two weeks ago and had since stabilized, the others fell in a larger percentage than KWEB itself did. In particular, 58.com ( WUBA ) dropped by double digits in percentage, more than returning the post-results gains on November 15.
IQ Price data by YCharts
Unsatisfactory Q3 Results And Downside Q4 Guidance From JD.com JD.com started the week on a poor note after it reported its Q3 2018 results that beat consensus estimates for EPS but missed on revenue. Those hoping for a Q4 pickup were also disappointed, as management guided for revenue to be in the CNY130-135 billion range, representing a growth rate between 18 percent and 23 percent compared with the fourth quarter of 2017, versus the consensus forecast at CNY135.95 billion. Despite trading at a price-to-sales ratio (on a trailing twelve-month basis) of only 0.42 times, the lowest in its trading history, the market is still not satisfied with the 21 percent year-on-year (YOY) increase in revenue it achieved for Q3.
JD PS Ratio (TTM) data by YCharts
A jump in the annual active customer accounts from 266.3 million last year to 305.2 million also did not help, as the market's attention was turned to the apparently slower growth, no thanks to a larger base. In addition, the margin picture is also not bright. While its non-GAAP gross profit margin was rather stable at 14.1 percent on a year-to-date (YTD) basis compared with the same period last year, 2018 could mark the first time in recent years that the margin did not improve YOY. The non-GAAP operating margin was even worse, dropping from 1.4 percent last year (2017 9M) to 0.5 percent YTD.
Source: JD.com Q3 2018 Earnings call slides
The weak results prompted several analysts to revise their price targets on JD.com downwards. Interestingly, despite a huge decline on the post-results downgrades, the consensus price target at $29.13 still reflects a substantial upside of 51 percent.
JD data by YCharts
The unresolved accusation on founder and CEO Richard Liu of raping a 21-year-old student is also not helping the stock price. A detailed Reuters report published on Thursday rekindled interest in the case. Based on my conversations with my Chinese friends, Richard's rags-to-riches story is now shattered by the high likelihood that he had committed acts of infidelity, whether the other party was consensual or not. This might not amount to anything, but the change in sentiment could result in some lost businesses, talents, and investors who want to take a stand against his infidelity.
Brighter Skies Ahead For JD.com While the third quarter was bad and the current quarter doesn't appear optimistic as well based on the guidance, 2019 could prove to be the turning point for JD.com. In response to questions regarding the company's growth strategy from analysts during the earnings conference call, Richard Liu provided several drivers for an improved net profit setup next year.
First, for those concerned about the ballooning R&D expenditure (9M 2018 88 percent higher yoy), the CEO said the R&D cost "might not increase" next year, as the company has since determined where to focus its R&D efforts.
Second, the net profitability of JD Logistics will be boosted "a lot". Despite the third quarter being a seasonally low one, the volume still increased on a sequential basis for its warehousing business, leading to a higher utilization and narrowing loss ratio consequently.
Third, Richard Liu guided that the company expects to grow faster than the industry average, resulting in a higher market share.
Fourth, for its 7Fresh stores, the CEO said the management is "actually pretty comfortable" that on a single-store basis the margin would be able to "breakeven and turn positive in a relatively short period of time".
In terms of cash flow, the CEO also said that he expects to see it improving "a lot" in 2019, since the heavy underwriting cost and logistics investment have already been incurred this year. The transfer of some logistic assets to a fund that has received "very good initial investor interest" is on track. The company anticipates a transaction to happen "in the first half of next year".
Richard Liu reiterated that he would "personally focus on four things; one is strategy, the other is culture, then team, and then new businesses". I expect the media, analysts, and investors alike to have much to chew on next year as the company reveals more about its strategy and new businesses.
Pinduoduo Is Attempting To Unseat JD.com To rub salt on its wounds, a relative newcomer to the e-commerce scene, Pinduoduo ( PDD ), reported results that pleased the market, sending its share price soaring. Smaller Chinese names like Baozun ( BZUN ), Qudian ( QD ), and Bilibili ( BILI ) also saw large price increases during the week.
BILI Price data by YCharts
With the valuation of JD.com shrinking and Pinduoduo seeing its share price rebounding from a recent low, the market capitalization gap between the two has narrowed. If Pinduoduo maintains its momentum while JD.com continues to fumble, the former would be able to surpass the latter in terms of market valuation and enterprise value in the near future.
PDD Market Cap data by YCharts
What Pinduoduo has on its side is its relative youth. Investors appear to be more tolerant of its losses due to the earlier stage of growth the company is supposedly in. Revenue soared to RMB3.4 billion in the third quarter of 2018, a seven-fold expansion, dwarfing the 21 percent increase achieved by JD.com. At the same time, the company's total operating expenses jumped 8.3 times to RMB3.9 billion, surpassing its revenue.
Shareholders might be attracted to the lean model that Pinduoduo is adopting, in sharp contrast with JD.com, which has invested heavily in its own logistics and warehousing assets. Pinduoduo sees itself as an "enabler" to its partners, including merchants, manufacturers, logistics providers, and other service providers.
In response to an analyst who asked a question about Pinduoduo's competitive strategy, Tian Xu, its Vice-President of Finance, replied that while it is "relatively easy" to emulate the platform user interface or group purchase feature, the head start and focus it has in offering customers "value for money products in a fun, social, dynamic shopping experience" helped differentiate it from copycats. The company executives repeatedly cited its in-house game app, Duo Duo Orchard, as an example of its strategy to provide users with a "differentiated and entertaining shopping experience", helping to increase and retain the mindshare of consumers.
Source: Inkstone
Unscathed By The Short-Selling Attack By Blue Orca Curiously, the recent rebound in the share price of Pinduoduo happened amid the backdrop of short-seller Blue Orca's accusation that the company under-reported costs, while overstating its revenue. Indeed, it beggars the question that if Alibaba ( BABA ) has fraudulently reported its financial results (i.e., they seem too good to be true), and Pinduoduo's numbers are way superior, should we be really worried about the authenticity? For instance, Blue Orca pointed out that Pinduoduo achieved a Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) of RMB167 million per employee, more than quadruple that of JD.com.
Source: Chart extracted from Blue Orca's report on Pinduoduo
Blue Orca also adopted the typical playbook of short-sellers, claiming huge discrepancies between what Pinduoduo reported in its SAIC filings, which include basic financial statements submitted by law to the Chinese government and the financial numbers disclosed to U.S. investors. For instance, it opined that the SAIC filings showed Pinduoduo's 2017 net losses incurred in China were 65 percent higher than those reported in its SEC filings.
During the recent earnings conference call, the VP of Finance concluded his prepared remarks with a brief response to the accusations. Unfortunately, there was no further elaboration on this topic subsequently in the Q&A session.
"Lastly, I would like to make a quick comment in response to claim that the company has misrepresented our revenues and earnings. I would to stress that we have always held ourselves to the highest standards and that the numbers in our consolidated financial statements are in compliance with the rules and regulations of the SEC.
Our filings are in accordance with U.S. GAAP and the audited financial statements included therein, have been audited by Ernst and Young. Similarly, our related party transactions, as included in the IPO prospectus, have also been disclosed in accordance with the U.S. securities laws, listing rules and NASDAQ regulations."
The Week Ahead - What To Watch Out For The highly discussed and anticipated meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at the G20 is finally happening within days. Speculations are rife on the possible outcomes for the meeting to be held on December 1. While much is at stake, most pundits are not expecting a conclusive trade deal to be hammered out during the meeting. It would probably suffice (i.e., enough for the market to rally) if President Trump expressively softens his rhetoric against China following the meet-up with President Xi.
In terms of earnings releases, Sina Corporation ( SINA ) would report its Q3 results pre-market on November 28. Historically, Sina has been able to beat the consensus estimates for every quarter since 2015. This means the market could be unforgiving if the results are anything but a positive surprise.
